plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: A herbaceous perennial with large, often fragrant, bowl-shaped to fully double blooms atop sturdy stems with deeply lobed glossy green foliage. It is a classic cottage garden favorite and can live for decades.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to China, Mongolia, and Siberia; widely cultivated in temperate gardens across North America and Europe
plants.funFact: Peonies are famously long-lived, with some plants continuing to bloom for over 50 years, and ants visiting the buds do not actually help them open.

plants.name: Rosa gallica
plants.description: One of the oldest cultivated roses, forming a suckering, thorny shrub with richly fragrant, semi-double flowers in deep pinks and crimsons with golden stamens. It is the ancestor of many garden roses.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Native to central and southern Europe and western Asia; grown in gardens in temperate regions worldwide
plants.funFact: Rosa gallica petals retain their fragrance when dried, so they were used for centuries in medicine, potpourri, and perfumery.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A medium to large tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often when the tree is nearly leafless. It lines streets in warm climates and carpets the ground with fallen blossoms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere subtropics (May to June); also blooms in October to November in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to South America (Argentina, Bolivia); planted in California, Mexico, Florida, the Mediterranean, South Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, the jacaranda bloom is so iconic that the city is nicknamed the Jacaranda City, with tens of thousands of trees lining its streets.

plants.name: Cypripedium reginae
plants.description: A striking native orchid with a pouch-shaped pink and white lip, hairy stems, and pleated leaves. It grows in bogs, fens, and damp woodland, and can take over a decade to flower from seed.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (late May to July)
plants.location: Northeastern and north-central North America, including Minnesota (state flower), Ontario, and the Great Lakes region
plants.funFact: This orchid can live for over 50 years, and it relies on a deceptive trap: bees enter the pouch and are forced to exit past the pollen, as there is no nectar reward.
